canonical_statement: For every continuous finite-dimensional real vector field defined on an open neighborhood U of initial data (t0, x0), there are epsilon > 0 and a curve x through x0 that stays in U and satisfies x'(t) = f(t, x(t)) within the closed interval [t0 - epsilon, t0 + epsilon], with one-sided derivatives at its endpoints.
domain_and_universes: n : Nat; time : Real; StateSpace n = Fin n -> Real with its standard finite-dimensional norm; U : Set (Real x StateSpace n); Prop in universe 0
ordered_binders: f : Real -> StateSpace n -> StateSpace n
hypotheses: the uncurried vector field p |-> f p.1 p.2 is ContinuousOn U
conclusion: There are epsilon > 0 and x with x t0 = x0 such that for every t in Set.Icc (t0 - epsilon) (t0 + epsilon), (t, x t) is in U and HasDerivWithinAt x (f t (x t)) on that interval at t.
